html:
The Battle of Gaugamela was fought on 1 October 331 BCE in northern Iraq, near today's Mosul and Erbil, between Alexander the Great and the Persian king Darius III. Alexander's victory decided the fall of the Persian Empire.

It was their second great battle. Darius had lost to Alexander at Issus in 333 BCE and fled. This time he gathered a much larger army from across his empire, with cavalry from Bactria, war elephants and chariots with blades fixed to their wheels. He chose a wide, flat plain and had it levelled so his chariots and horsemen could use their numbers.

Alexander's army of Macedonians and Greeks was smaller. He led his cavalry out to the right, at an angle, and Persian horsemen rode out to follow, which opened a gap in the Persian line. Alexander turned and charged through it with his Companion cavalry, straight at Darius. Darius fled, as he had at Issus. On the other wing the Macedonian general Parmenion held on under heavy pressure until the Persian army broke.

What followed:

  • Alexander took Babylon and Susa without a fight, and then the Persian royal city of Persepolis, which he burned.
  • Darius fled east and was murdered in 330 BCE by his own satrap, Bessus.

Gaugamela turned Alexander's conquests from a raid into the takeover of a world empire. The numbers on the Persian side given by ancient writers are much exaggerated, and historians still argue about the true sizes of both armies.
sum: The Battle of Gaugamela was fought on 1 October 331 BCE in northern Iraq, near today's Mosul and Erbil, between Alexander the Great and the Persian king Darius III. Alexander's victory decided the fall of the Persian Empire.
